Team Name: CLA 1, Moon Farmers 
Team #: 16299 
Challenge Division: Elementary 
Team Members: Seraphine Potts, Karleigh Long, Jack Powell, Xane Long, Ledger Ward 
Team Facilitators: Kitty Ward, Beverly Mouton (Roi S Wood Campus, Joplin School District, 
Joplin MO) 
 
How do additives affect Green Bean growth in 
Lunar Simulant? 
Background: We chose to try several different ratios of commercial potting soil, lunar simulant 
(which we refer to as ‘moon dust’), perlite, sand. With some of our pots, we added osmocote to 
help facilitate growth. Our thinking with the sand and perlite was that the perlite would lighten 
the weight of the soil and therefore make it act more like the weight of the soil on the moon. We 
obviously have no way to test this, but thought it would be a good addition to our experiment. 
We used the same thinking with the sand since it would make the soil heavier. We wanted to 
see which soil would grow better, heavy or light. We also have several ratios of simulant to soil, 
to test which ratio was the best growing medium. We randomly assigned ratios to our pots. 
 
Independent Variables: Our independent variables were the ratios of the following in each pot: 
Moon Simulant, Potting Soil, Perlite, Sand, Osmocote. 
Each of our pots had different ratios and not all the same substances were put in each pot. Our 
thinking was that we could use perlite to simulate lighter soil to account for less gravity on the 
moon. We also were thinking that sand would make the soil heavier if needed on the moon. 
The potting soil has organic matter in it to accommodate for the lack of organic matter in the 
moon simulant. And finally we thought the osmocote could give our green bean plants a little 
boost. Also we measured how much water we used to water the plants (¼ cup every week at 
the beginning, but every other day as the plants began to grow) 
 
Dependent Variables: Each week we measured the following: Plant height, # of leaves, # of 
blossoms, # of successful blossoms (bean pods). 
 
Control: Our control plant was 50% soil and 50% moon simulant. (no other substances)

Our Hypothesis:Based on our understanding that the lunar soil had no organic matter, we 
hypothesized that the combination of substances in pot #2 would yield the most growth and 
produce. 
 
Our Procedures and Measurements: We measured our plants each Friday. We measured the 
height of each plant, we counted the number of leaves, we counted the number of blossoms 
and the number of successful blossoms (green beans). We watered the plants each week at 
the beginning of the experiment, but at the plants grew we increased the watering schedule to 
every other day. 
 
What Happened?: Our hypothesis turned out to be wrong. We found that Pot #7 was the most 
productive pot and the only one to produce a green bean. We also observed that Pot # 10 (the 
pot with only moon simulant and osmocote actually grew beyond germination, which we didn’t 
expect. Several of our observations and comments about these results were: “I think the 
astronauts should take osmocote to enhance the growth of the plants, it’s lighter and takes up 
less space than soil” and “Since #7 is the productive one, this should be the ratio that the 
astronauts use”. We also found out that as the plants grew, the PH levels in the soil decreased.
